title: Two-term horocycle-average asymptotics with Holder coefficient functions for complementary-series Casimir eigenfunctions on compact PSL(2,R) quotients
source_title: Asymptotics and limit theorems for horocycle ergodic integrals à la Ratner (with an appendix by Emilio Corso)
author: Davide Ravotti
difficulty_reason: The Casimir equation must first be converted into a forced ODE for renormalized horocycle integrals with uniform control of the forcing. The source identifies global coefficient integrals and tracks the two complementary-series exponents while estimating the tail to obtain the inverse-time remainder and explicit average bound. It then controls anisotropic geodesic expansion inside those coefficient integrals to prove the exact Holder exponents, a substantive dynamics obligation beyond solving a scalar constant-coefficient ODE.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Only Theorem1(iii), 0<mu<1/4, C2 Casimir eigenfunction, compact quotient by a uniform lattice, normalized invariant probability and nu=sqrt(1-4mu). Coefficient exponents and explicit sup/remainder/average bounds remain exact. Read full ODE derivation11–13, complementary-series formulas14–15 and regularity15–16. Lemma10 last display bounds a sum of two explicit positive terms by a single max coefficient; that numerical constant is not part of selected theorem, whose Holder assertion is qualitative. The preceding fully written split-integral estimate supplies the required O(r^a) directly. Preserve literal display and bound this as ancillary constant simplification, not a new dynamics proof or alteration of source constants. No principal/double-root/discrete/spatial/temporal variants separately counted. Main author Davide Ravotti; Emilio Corso is explicitly credited for the unselected appendix.
